_comment: The Yamaha CP-80's baseline for tools/cp_model.py: everything the documents give, and what physics derives from them, before any recording. Each value's source: [S] the service manual / schematic / parts list (yamaha_cp80_sm.pdf, yamaha_CP_80_wiring.pdf, the CP-70B service manual for the CP-70 column), [C] fitted to the service manual's calibration levels (one point per setting: the shape between is assumed), [P] physics from [S] values with a stated assumption, [A] assumed (typical of acoustic pianos or of the parts): to be measured on recordings.

tuning_cents._src: [S] sm p14: the CP-80 tuning table, A49 = 440 Hz, the stretch of each key's sounding pitch

strings._src: [S] parts list p28: keys 1-22 one wound string, 23-42 two wound, 43-88 plain music wire (two each: [S] the 70B manual, 16-73 two strings) of these gauges

gauge_mm._src: [S] piano wire numbering: #13 = 0.775 mm, 0.025 mm a half number

stress_frac._src: [A] the plain strings' tension as a share of the wire's strength (pianos: 0.3..0.6)

wound._src: [A] the case is 1460 x 1006 mm ([S]): A0's speaking length about 1 m; wound tensions 700..1100 N

b_wound_from_stretch._src: [P] B of keys 1..42 from the tuning table's octave stretch: the geometric mean of a 2:1 octave (2597 B cents) and a 4:2 (10388 B)

detune_cents._src: [A] a pair's two strings: 0.3..2 cents apart in tuned pianos

undamped_first._src: [S] parts list p18-20: damper heads on keys 1..73 only

decay._src: [M] each partial's loss sigma(f) = b1 + b2 f + b3 f^2 (1/s; T60 = 6.91 / sigma), fitted to the decays of a CP-70's DI recording (frodhes-refs audio/cp70-yt, YouTube 'I Bought a Yamaha CP70!' 0:01-3:02: 38 chord tails, 0.35 s after the onset to the next one, the median slope per octave band 200-6400 Hz: T60 29.7 / 22.2 / 13.7 / 10.3 / 5.5 s; the fit within 0.5 dB/s). Chords, maybe the pedal, a lossy stream: the order is sure, the values to be checked on single notes. The grand-piano prior it replaces: T60 18 s (A0) .. 0.6 s (C8), 8x faster in the middle (no soundboard: the strings lose far less).

hammer._src: [S] hammers of urethane rubber covered by artificial leather (sm p2; 70B: synthetic buckskin over hard rubber), 6 hammer types by range (parts p22), blow 40 mm (sm p16). [A] the felt law F = K x^p with a harder K than felt, the masses and the strike position: grand-piano values.
hammer.k_mid_src: [M] 16x the grand-felt prior (3e9): the long-term spectrum of a CP-70 chord passage then matches Wingate's DI within 2.5 dB up to 4 kHz (-6 dB at 8 kHz; Hollow Sun's and Amazound's demos agree with that DI at 4-8 kHz); rubber under leather is harder than felt

contact_ms_lit._src: [A] grand pianos at mf (Askenfelt & Jansson 1990, Hall 1986): ~4 ms bass, ~2 ms mid, <0.5 ms top; rubber is harder: shorter

pickup._src: [S] a piezo per note under the bridge, all 88 in parallel on one bus (no trim); it reads the string's force on the bridge, T dy/dx. [S] keys 83-88 through a 0.022 uF series capacitor: [A] its divider unknown (the piezos' capacitance), 0 dB here.

voicing._src: [A] every key at the same level at vel 80 (a smooth gain over the keys). The physics gives the top octave ~18 dB under the middle; the schematic says the real top was too loud instead (the 0.022 uF in series with keys 83-88 can only lower them): Yamaha voiced the hammers / piezos for an even output. To be measured.

preamp._src: [S] the TR board: FET1 (input 470 k, C101 0.1 uF), the passive BASS / MIDDLE / TREBLE network, BRILLIANCE, FET2, the FET3 Sallen-Key low-pass (R111 = R112 = 39 k, C106 2200 pF, C108 470 pF: CP-80; 1000 pF: CP-70B), FET4/5, the two LDR channels, VOLUME. Modelled linear (-32 dBm in: the JFETs' distortion is far under the strings').

cal._src: [S] sm p11-12, input -32 dBm. Relative to 500 Hz with VR2-VR4 at max, BRILLIANCE MEDIUM (J01 -31 dBm): 50 Hz bass max -17 (+14), bass min -34 (-3); 5 kHz treble max -23 (+8), treble min -35.5 (-4.5); all at 5, 5 kHz -29.5 (+1.5); BRILLIANCE HIGH -24 (+5.5 over MEDIUM), LOW -41.5 (-12)

cal_cp70._src: [S] the CP-70B service manual p13-14, the same procedure (500 Hz reference -31 dBm [A]: not printed there): 50 Hz bass max -16.5 (+14.5), bass min -34.5 (-3.5); 5 kHz treble max -25 (+6), treble min -40 (-9). No centre point: the CP-80's centre gains

bass_shelf_hz._src: [A] the BASS shelf's corner (the calibration has 50 Hz only)

middle._src: [A] VR3 is 1 k against R134 3.9 k: a small range; no calibration point

tremolo._src: [S] a Wien-bridge oscillator (C 2.2 uF, R 5.6 k + VR6 100 k: 0.69..12.9 Hz; spec 0.8..10 Hz), 5 V zeners soft-limit it; two MCD527 LED/LDR shunts in antiphase (ch1 / ch2) over 22 k series resistors; depth 15 % (min) .. 40 % (max) and more (spec). [A] the LDR's 3 / 35 ms response (as the 200A's) and the soft limit's 3rd harmonic.

cp70._src: [S] the CP-70/70B: 73 keys E1..E7, keys 1-15 one wound string, 16-37 two wound, then plain #17..#14; the SK low-pass with C108 1000 pF; no BRILLIANCE
